Maintenance Report — MNT-0168-005

Asset: WELL-0168 (NE-08 Well 168, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 30 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 30 Jun 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0168-0037 on 2023-06-29 Report written: 30 Jun 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0168-0037 at 15:45 on 2023-06-29 found crude oil on the pad: about 10.5% of the pad area, estimated 6.2 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 229 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 183 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.7 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0168-005 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.33% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0168-018

Asset: WELL-0168 (NE-08 Well 168, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 24 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 02 Sep 2025 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 230 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0168-0148 on 2025-08-21 Report written: 02 Sep 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0168-0148 showed the wellhead at 36.7 °C with the air at 30.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Electric motor (exchange unit)4,426
V-belts885
Electrical connectors590
Labour (company crew and contractor)2,879
Total8,780

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 4 ppm
WS-07MetWritten the same day as the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.
